    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401481/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I have a testing world where I build everything and have had it for many years now. I was playing modded with forge yesterday and accidentally clicked on my testing world rather than my modded one, thought nothing of it until I came back today to test out something new with redstone.</p>
<p>When I clicked on the world using the optifine loader, I was greeted with a message. "Errors in currently selected data packs prevented the world from loading. You can either try to load it with the vanilla data pack ("safe mode"), or go back to the title screen and fix it manually."</p>
<p>I have scoured forums and have yet to find a solution to my problem. Somehow in the last few years I have never made a single save to the world so I have nothing to back it up to. Also, when I check the data packs folder nothing is in there. Any help would be nice.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I have a testing world where I build everything and have had it for many years now. I was playing modded with forge yesterday and accidentally clicked on my testing world rather than my modded one, thought nothing of it until I came back today to test out something new with redstone.</p>
<p>When I clicked on the world using the optifine loader, I was greeted with a message. "Errors in currently selected data packs prevented the world from loading. You can either try to load it with the vanilla data pack ("safe mode"), or go back to the title screen and fix it manually."</p>
<p>I have scoured forums and have yet to find a solution to my problem. Somehow in the last few years I have never made a single save to the world so I have nothing to back it up to. Also, when I check the data packs folder nothing is in there. Any help would be nice.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've managed to spawn <em>inside</em> the End Island, causing an immediate crash on startup.</p>
<p>I've attempted to modify my <code>dimension</code> and <code>pos</code> in my playerdata, but no matter what I set it to, the next time I log in I'm back at 0,9,0 and triggering the immediate crash again.</p>
<p>I've even tried setting spawnForce to 1.</p>
<p>What next?  Why is the UUID.dat file being ignored, then overwritten?</p>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401493/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>In singleplayer worlds, the player data stored in <code>Player</code> key of the <code>level.dat</code> file itself overrides the player data stored in the <code>playerdata/&lt;UUID&gt;.dat</code> files. You need to edit the former file to actually change your position.</p>
<p>See <a href="https://minecraft.fandom.com/wiki/Java_Edition_level_format#level.dat_format" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Minecraft Wiki</a></p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>I've even tried setting spawnForce to 1.</p>
<p>What next?  Why is the UUID.dat file being ignored, then overwritten?</p>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>In singleplayer worlds, the player data stored in <code>Player</code> key of the <code>level.dat</code> file itself overrides the player data stored in the <code>playerdata/&lt;UUID&gt;.dat</code> files. You need to edit the former file to actually change your position.</p>
<p>See <a href="https://minecraft.fandom.com/wiki/Java_Edition_level_format#level.dat_format" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Minecraft Wiki</a></p>
</div>

<p>I've even tried setting spawnForce to 1.</p>
<p>What next?  Why is the UUID.dat file being ignored, then overwritten?</p>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>In singleplayer worlds, the player data stored in <code>Player</code> key of the <code>level.dat</code> file itself overrides the player data stored in the <code>playerdata/&lt;UUID&gt;.dat</code> files. You need to edit the former file to actually change your position.</p>
<p>See <a href="https://minecraft.fandom.com/wiki/Java_Edition_level_format#level.dat_format" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Minecraft Wiki</a></p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401560/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401560/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401560/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401560/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401538/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401560/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401560/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401558/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>
